name: stat
title: Stat
description: Every number a player reads: score, timer, lives, streak, rank, multiplier, level and XP, from one component with a different kind. Tabular numerals so a changing digit does not shift the row, an optional label, an optional change beside it, and `data-gs-value` carrying the machine-readable number alongside whatever is rendered, so a test reads 90 while a player reads 1:30. Critical changes the fill, a glyph and the weight at once, never colour alone. Performs nothing: it does not count down, fetch or decide when a value is critical. It does not award points or settle a value; the host supplies the number and any settlement state. Use it directly when the host chooses the kind at runtime, needs a rank, level or XP number, or already owns a clock and only needs its seconds displayed. Use `score`, `multiplier`, `timer`, `round`, `lives` or `streak` when the number has that fixed meaning, so the host does not have to remember its kind. The wrappers let a test identify the number among others: score, timer, round, lives and streak have their own `data-gs-component`, while multiplier defaults to `stat` and is identified by `data-gs-stat="multiplier"`. Reach for `timer` when the component must run the clock; setting `kind="timer"` on stat never starts one. Since the presentation prop it also owns the silhouette: plain, chip, pill, dots or pips. The design draws six game-state objects as six shapes and the library drew all six as a label above a number on the page background, so a player reading a HUD could not tell the timer from the score except by the word. The prop changes the shape and nothing else — same number, same accessible name, same states, same attributes — which is why it is a prop rather than five components. dots and pips additionally draw a row of marks from the same value and max the number already carries, so nothing is a second place the number is written down.
docs: Pass `kind` to say which number this is; it picks the word and the token scale and nothing else. Pass `format` to render a value as something other than the bare number, and `data-gs-value` still carries the real one. Pass `settlement="optimistic"` for a local render the host has yet to confirm, and `"corrected"` when the host disagrees with what the player already saw. `score`, `timer`, `lives` and `streak` are this component, not four components.
